[TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r2] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | One cause is the story’s prominence among People of the Book: Quraysh learned it from them, and its Christian images and monuments spread it widely, so communities reshaped it to fit their beliefs.
[TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r3] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | A second cause is Muslims’ broad collection of outside reports, especially through converts such as Wahb ibn Munabbih and Kaʿb al-Aḥbār; later transmitters treated such material as prophetic reports.
